tasks.q: Which of these should be considered before a new technology is released? Select all that apply.
opts: Who might be harmed by it
What it does to the environment
Whether it widens the gap between rich and poor
The font used in the manual
correct: Who might be harmed by it
What it does to the environment
Whether it widens the gap between rich and poor
tasks.fb: Every one of those is an impact the specification asks you to consider.

tasks.q: What is the difference between a legal issue and an ethical issue?
a: Legal is what the law allows; ethical is what is right, which can be stricter
Ethical issues only apply to companies
tasks.fb: Something can be perfectly legal and still be wrong.

tasks.q: Which of these is an ethical question rather than a legal one?
a: Should a company use AI to decide who gets a job interview?
Is copying a film without paying illegal?
What does the Data Protection Act require?
Which licence does this software use?
tasks.fb: Legal questions have answers in law. Ethical ones are arguments.

tasks.q: Is each concern mainly ethical or mainly legal?
items: Should a shop's cameras recognise faces?
Ethical
Is it illegal to use someone else's login?
Legal
Should children's data be sold to advertisers?
Ethical
Does copying this image break copyright?
Legal
Should a driverless car protect its passenger or a pedestrian?
Ethical
Must a company report a data breach?
Legal
tasks.fb: Legal questions are settled by an Act of Parliament; ethical ones are argued.

tasks.q: Which is the strongest exam answer about school monitoring software?
a: It protects pupils by flagging harmful searches, but records private messages too, so schools must say exactly what is stored
tasks.fb: Both sides, a reason each, and a position at the end.

tasks.q: Why do these questions carry high marks in the exam?
a: They ask you to weigh competing points and reach a justified conclusion
tasks.fb: Marks come from the reasoning, not the length.

tasks.q: A supermarket replaces half its staffed tills with self-service machines. How is each group affected?
tasks.fb: The same change can benefit one group and cost another their job. Both belong in your answer.
tasks.title: Self-service tills: who is affected?
tasks.note: Tap each cell to choose: no real effect, benefits, or loses out.

tasks.q: Why should an answer name several stakeholders?
a: Because a change rarely affects everyone the same way, and the marks are for showing that
Because the exam says to name five
So you can avoid a conclusion

tasks.q: Is each point an argument for or against piracy?
items: The creator is paid nothing for their work
Against
Some films are not available legally in every country
For
Studios take fewer risks on new ideas
Against
Subscriptions cost more than some people can afford
For
It is illegal under copyright law
Against
Copying a file costs the maker nothing extra
For
tasks.fb: A strong answer uses points from both columns, then commits to a view.

tasks.q: Which sentence is a justified conclusion?
a: On balance it is wrong, because the creator loses the income that funds the next piece of work
tasks.fb: A position plus the reason that decided it.

tasks.q: Put these parts of a strong impact answer in order.
steps: Name the kind of impact the question is about
Give the arguments on both sides, with reasons
Reach a conclusion and justify it
tasks.fb: Same structure every time, whatever the technology.

tasks.q: An answer lists ten disadvantages and no advantages. What is missing?
a: The other side of the argument, and a justified conclusion

tasks.q: Which kind of impact is each concern?
items: A phone contains metals mined in dangerous conditions
Environmental
An app shares your location with advertisers
Privacy
Using someone else's password to read their email
Legal
Should AI decide who gets a loan?
Ethical
Old laptops dumped in landfill leak toxic metals
Environmental
A company keeps customer data for twenty years
Privacy
Copying a game and selling it at a car boot sale
Legal
Should delivery drivers be tracked every minute?
Ethical
tasks.fb: Many real cases are two or three of these at once: say so in the exam.

info.title: Why this topic exists
info.text: Every specification now includes impacts, because the people building systems are the ones who decide what gets built. The technical skill is only half the job.

info.title: Trolley problems
info.text: Driverless cars force a decision nobody wants to write down: who a car should protect in a crash. Engineers really do have to choose.

info.title: Marks for arguing
info.text: Impact questions are among the highest-mark questions on the paper, and the marks are for reasoning rather than recall.

info.title: Stakeholders in law
info.text: Big public projects legally require consultation with the people affected, which is stakeholder analysis by another name.

info.title: Piracy figures
info.text: Studies on lost income disagree wildly, partly because not every copy would have been a sale. Be careful quoting numbers you can't check.

info.title: Your turn
info.text: Every technology you use was signed off by someone. The questions in this topic are the ones they were asked.
